items.title: TOGO import substitutes G_PER_L for volume units: 3,803 rows, of which 1,224 are non-water and numerically wrong
items.body:
Found while verifying the source spelling for #406 — the raw TOGO capture is
tracked, so the import can be compared against it directly.

## The substitution

`data/raw/togo/togo_media.json` records each component's own unit. Comparing
2,900 matched TOGO media, component by component:

```
comparable rows                                32,841
source unit is a VOLUME (ml, ml/l, L, ul)       3,808
  -> recorded as G_PER_L                        3,803
  -> recorded as ML_PER_L or L                      2
```

The unit is not converted, it is **replaced**. `CultureMech:008849`
(`TOGO:M2262`, PCR-S11 medium) side by side with its source:

| ingredient | TOGO says | record says |
|---|---|---|
| Seawater (autoclaved) | 1000 **ml** | 1000 **G_PER_L** |
| Trace metals 'Gaffron+Se' | 0.5 **ml/l** | 0.5 **G_PER_L** |
| 50mM NaH2PO4 | 100 **ml** | 100 **G_PER_L** |
| 0.1N HCl | 40 **ml** | 40 **G_PER_L** |
| (NH4)2SO4 | 400 uM | 400 MICROMOLAR ✅ |
| Vitamin B12 | 10 ug/L | 10 MICROG_PER_L ✅ |
| Hepes | 119.15 g | 119.15 G_PER_L ✅ |

Molar and mass units convert correctly. Only volumes are mislabelled, and the
schema already has `ML_PER_L` and `L` for them.

## Where it is and is not defensible

**Water — 2,579 rows.** Water's density is 1, so `1000 ml -> 1000 g/L` is
numerically near-exact. Ugly, and it is what feeds `WATER_AS_VOLUME` in
`audit-concentration-plausibility`, but not a wrong quantity.

**Everything else — 1,224 rows across 751 records.** The density is not 1, so
the number itself is wrong:

| ingredient | rows | density | error |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `HCl (25%; 7.7 M)` | 72 | ~1.12 | 12% low |
| `Methanol` | 26 | 0.792 | 26% high |
| `Glycerol` | 21 | 1.26 | 21% low |
| `Tween 80` | 20 | 1.06 | |
| `Ethanol` | 14 | 0.789 | 27% high |
| `Sol. 1`, `Artificial seawater`, `Seawater`, `NaOH 1 N`, ... | | | |

`0.5 ml/l` of a trace-metal stock recorded as `0.5 g/L` is not a rounding
difference — it is a different physical quantity, and nothing downstream can
tell.

## No gate sees the non-water half

`audit-concentration-plausibility` has `WATER_AS_VOLUME` (water >= 1000 G_PER_L),
which is why the water rows are already inside #150's backlog. Methanol at
`792 G_PER_L`, glycerol at `50 G_PER_L` and HCl at `40 G_PER_L` match no
detector — not a trace salt, not an indicator, not water.

## Suggested

1. Map source volume units onto `ML_PER_L` / `L` at import rather than
   defaulting to `G_PER_L`. The enum values exist.
2. Repair the 1,224 non-water rows from the tracked raw capture, which holds
   the original unit — so this is a relabelling, not a re-derivation, and needs
   no source lookup.
3. Decide the water case deliberately: `2,579` rows are numerically fine and
   semantically wrong, and they currently inflate `WATER_AS_VOLUME`.
4. Check whether the same substitution exists in the other volume-bearing
   importers (MediaDive, KOMODO, JCM) — this was found by comparing against a
   tracked raw capture, which not every source has.

Related: #150 (the plausibility backlog the water half sits in), #381 (absolute
amounts with no representable unit), #394 (a different import-time arithmetic
defect), #406 (the record this was found from).

items.title: Preparation instructions are parsed as ingredients with concentrations
items.body:
Noticed while canarying #263's dedup.

`data/normalized_yaml/algae/sbbm.yaml` carried this as an ingredient row:

```yaml
- preferred_term: Make up to 1 litre with distilled water. For agar add
  concentration:
    value: '15'
    unit: G_PER_L
  source: CCAP Medium MR_SBBM.pdf
```

That is a preparation instruction from the source PDF, parsed as an ingredient and given
the concentration of whatever followed it (the 15 g/l is presumably the agar). It appeared
twice, which is how the dedup pass surfaced it.

Two distinct harms:

1. **A phantom ingredient.** Anything counting ingredients, exporting to KG-Microbe, or
   computing composition sees a component that does not exist.
2. **A misattributed concentration.** If the 15 g/l belongs to agar, then agar is either
   missing its concentration or carrying a different one — worth checking which.

This is likely not one record. Candidate detection: `preferred_term` containing a verb
phrase, sentence punctuation, or exceeding some length — real ingredient names are short
noun phrases. A quick scan for `preferred_term` values containing `. ` or more than ~6
words would size it.

Related: #265 (ingredient synonyms effectively unpopulated) and #259 (`term.label` carrying
ingredient strings) are both symptoms of the same underlying thing — the ingredient field
is absorbing text it was not meant to hold.

items.title: Repair recipe browsing, evidence, diagrams, and verified source navigation
items.body:
Recipe pages now expose existing growth evidence, target organisms and variants; provenance, review rows and merged sources link only to verified current identities. Search accepts readable names and identifiers, mobile filters remain reachable, Back restores the actual result set, and theme labels reflect the next action. Composition diagrams render in an isolated sandbox with their own style policy while the record CSP stays strict.

Both retained maps fit narrow and desktop screens, disclose their snapshot scope and actual counts, and navigate through verified current record identities. Coordinates and embedded point data are unchanged; unresolved historical identities are explicit. The growth review is rebuilt from all 15,910 normalized records and distinguishes missing local proposal artifacts from unreviewed science.

One source-backed scientific correction changes 2ASW's NaNO/Azimilide assignment to NaNO3/sodium nitrate (CHEBI:63005). The current official CCAP revision 002, approved 29 May 2026, and ChEBI support the correction. The retained 15 g/L is explicitly a stock concentration. The exact April-import PDF was not recovered from the repository source inventory, including ignored files, so historical version equivalence is not claimed. The guarded normalized write appends actual Codex curation history; its merged singleton is regenerated through RecipeMerger.

Validation: the required fast suite passed 6,822 tests (16 skipped); 15 artifact-inventory tests and strict validation of the corrected recipe passed. All 15,910 normalized and 6,320 merged pages were regenerated, and web coverage is complete. Chromium checks cover real Back/reload behavior, both diagram themes, responsive maps, unresolved identities and keyboard controls; independent review passed. The optional full suite was interrupted and is not reported as passing. The product gate passes under its configured policy (2,004 canonical, 274,684 ID-only, 29 accepted exceptions, 95,972 skipped/no-adapter rows, and 91 nonblocking warnings); this is not universal canonical-label validation. Whole-corpus merge integrity still fails on 1,247 duplicate-name groups and 3,286 fingerprint mismatches that predate this branch. Its only changed merged file has a correct fingerprint; no new duplicate names or fingerprint failures are introduced. The completed freshness audit finds 6,320 tracked versus 6,461 freshly generated merged recipes (1,128 unchanged, 1,469 changed, 3,723 tracked-only and 3,864 fresh-only). That broad corpus drift was already documented; this PR preserves unrelated records. Deployed rendering awaits publication.

items.title: cleanup_media_quality summed duplicate ingredient rows: 292 agar rows are physically impossible and no gate sees them
items.body:
Found while triaging #283, which turns out to be one instance of a much larger
pattern.

## The mutator

`scripts/cleanup_media_quality.py:149` merges duplicate ingredient rows by
**adding their concentrations**:

```python
total = sum(concentrations)
...
base['notes'] += f' [Merged {len(group)} duplicates: {", ".join(map(str, concentrations))}]'
```

It records exactly what it did, which is how this was findable:

```yaml
- preferred_term: Agar
  concentration: {value: '50.0', unit: G_PER_L}
  notes: ' (for solid medium) [Merged 3 duplicates: 15.0, 15.0, 20.0]'
```

15 + 15 + 20 = 50.

## Why summing is the wrong operation here

Duplicate rows for one ingredient usually mean the *same* addition was listed
twice by the importer, not that the medium receives the ingredient twice.
Summing turns a transcription artifact into a fabricated quantity.

For agar it is unambiguous. Agar is a solidifier that sets at **15-20 g/L**;
above roughly 30 g/L the medium will not pour and the value cannot be real.

```
Agar, G_PER_L, corpus-wide:
   2132 rows @ 15.0     <- normal
    574 rows @ 20       <- normal
    186 rows @ 50.0     <- 15+15+20
     65 rows @ 65.0
  ...
  rows above 30 g/L: 292
```

## Scale

| | count |
|---|--:|
| ingredient rows carrying a `[Merged N duplicates: ...]` note | **5,081** |
| ...across records | **2,667** |
| ...whose value equals the **sum** of the listed parts | **4,503** |
| agar rows above 30 g/L | **292** |
| records where a merged row **coexists** with another row of the same name | **276** |

Most affected ingredients: NaCl (981), Distilled water (840), CaCl2 x 2 H2O
(662), MgSO4 x 7 H2O (417), Agar (267).

That last row of the table is a second defect on top of the first: the merge
left a row behind, so `KOMODO_457_MINERAL_MEDIUM_BRUNNER.yaml` carries **both**
`Agar 50.0` and `Agar 15.0`. Whatever consumes it double-counts.

## Not all of it is wrong, which is the difficulty

`JCM_J151_PYROCOCCUS_MEDIUM` has `NaCl 14.85 = 13.85 + 1.0`, which may be a
legitimate total of two additions. `MnCl2 x 4 H2O 0.1018 = 0.0018 + 0.1` is a
trace element summed with what looks like a stock-strength value, and is not.
So this is not a blanket revert — the provable subset is where the summed value
is physically impossible for the substance.

## No gate sees it

`audit-concentration-plausibility` has three detectors — `WATER_AS_VOLUME`,
`TRACE_SALT_AS_STOCK`, `INDICATOR_UNIT_SLIP`. Agar is neither a trace salt nor
an indicator, and 50 g/L is below the water threshold. Confirmed: **zero rows
whose ingredient is agar appear in `concentration_plausibility.tsv`.**

The other two PR-blocking gates (`validate-strict`, `check-chebi-grounding`)
check shape and grounding, not plausibility of a value against its substance.

## Proposed work

1. A detector for duplicate ingredient rows within one record, classifying
   exact duplicates, power-of-ten pairs (#283), and merged-sum survivors.
2. A solidifier plausibility detector, so an impossible agar value fails rather
   than passing three green gates.
3. Repair only the provable subset. The agar case has a defensible target — the
   note preserves the original parts, so the pre-merge value is recoverable
   from the record itself without inventing anything.
4. Fix `cleanup_media_quality.py` so it cannot do this again.

Relates to #283 (one record of pattern 1), #150 (the plausibility backlog this
should not silently inflate), and #302 (why a total-based ratchet would hide a
repair here).

items.title: Stop summing duplicate ingredient rows, and undo it where the value is provable (#394)
items.body:
Closes #394. Found while triaging #283, which turns out to be one record of a
much larger pattern.

## The defect

`scripts/cleanup_media_quality.py:149` merged duplicate ingredient rows by
**adding** their concentrations — and recorded what it did, which is the only
reason any of this is recoverable:

```yaml
- preferred_term: Agar
  concentration: {value: '50.0', unit: G_PER_L}
  notes: ' (for solid medium) [Merged 3 duplicates: 15.0, 15.0, 20.0]'
```

Agar sets at **15-20 g/L**; at 50 the medium will not pour. `Methanol 1584.0
g/L` came from `792.0, 792.0` — above the density of methanol, so the source
listed neat solvent twice.

Duplicate rows almost always mean the importer transcribed one addition twice,
not that the medium receives the ingredient twice. Summing turned a
transcription artifact into a fabricated quantity.

| | count |
|---|--:|
| rows carrying a `[Merged N duplicates: …]` note | **5,081** across 2,667 records |
| …whose value is the **sum** of the listed parts | **4,503** |
| agar rows above 30 g/L | **292** |
| records where a merged row **coexists** with another row of the same name | **276** |

Nothing caught any of it: `audit-concentration-plausibility`'s three detectors
are `WATER_AS_VOLUME`, `TRACE_SALT_AS_STOCK`, `INDICATOR_UNIT_SLIP` — agar is
neither a trace salt nor an indicator, and 50 is below the water threshold.
**Zero rows whose ingredient is agar appear in `concentration_plausibility.tsv`.**

## What this changes

**1. The mutator stops summing.** When every duplicate agrees it collapses to
that value. When they disagree it keeps the first and raises a warning, because
which value the medium means is a question about the source recipe rather than
arithmetic.

**2. A gate.** `just audit-merged-duplicates`, added to the
concentration-plausibility workflow — it shares that workflow's path filter
exactly and guards the same property, a concentration that is not a real
measurement.

Three **independent** baselines, not one total (#302):

| detector | baseline | why |
|---|--:|---|
| `IDENTICAL_PARTS` | **0** | mechanically repairable; a nonzero count is a new import re-introducing the defect |
| `DIFFERING_PARTS` | 3772 | needs the source recipe; ratchet down as curation lands |
| `COEXISTING_ROW` | 276 | a merge survivor sharing a record with another row of the same name |

A single total would let a repair in one class pay for a regression in another,
and these three have different remedies.

**3. The repair.** 731 rows across 648 records where every merged part was the
same value — the pre-merge value is then the one distinct part, with no source
lookup and no arithmetic. `IDENTICAL_PARTS` goes **731 → 0**.

## What it deliberately does not do

The 3,772 rows whose merged parts **differ** are untouched. Choosing 15 or 20
out of `15.0, 15.0, 20.0` is curation, and a plausible guess that round-trips is
still false chemistry. They keep failing the audit until a source says which.

Not every sum is even wrong — `NaCl 14.85 = 13.85 + 1.0` may be a legitimate
total of two additions. That ambiguity is exactly why the repair is confined to
the provable half.

## Verification

- Across all 648 changed records: no top-level key changed, **no unit changed**,
  no ingredient field other than the collapsed value and its note changed, and
  `curation_history` gained exactly one event per file.
- `audit-concentration-plausibility` **dropped** 9,688 → 9,664 rows and
  3,516 → 3,493 records, because some collapsed values fall below a detector
  threshold. Ratchet **tightened** to 9,664 rather than left slack.
- Gates: `validate-strict` 0 errors / 15,877 files; `assign-ids-check`,
  `check-chebi-grounding`, `audit-merged-duplicates` all exit 0.
- `test-fast` 1464 passed.
- Non-vacuous: restoring the summing fails the three mutator tests (verified —
  `3 failed, 19 passed`).
- The repair is idempotent, and a repaired row stops being a finding without the
  evidence being erased (the note becomes `Collapsed N identical duplicates`).

## Follow-ups this exposes

- **#283** is one instance of the wider duplicate-row family; the 496 records
  carrying a repeated `(name, unit)` at differing values are a superset of what
  `COEXISTING_ROW` sees.
- The 3,772 `DIFFERING_PARTS` rows are a new curation lane, adjacent to #150.
- No plausibility detector knows what a **solidifier** is, which is why 292
  impossible agar rows passed three green gates.

items.title: Remove ingredient rows duplicated verbatim within a record (#263)
items.body:
Closes #263 — after correcting what that issue claimed.

## The filed cause was wrong

I filed #263 attributing all 34 anchor-carrying records to the shallow-copy bug fixed in
#261. That accounts for **17**. The other 17 are a different, more serious problem, and the
anchors are a symptom rather than the defect:

| shape | records |
|---|---:|
| aliased nested `term` dicts (the `split_parts` bug) | 17 |
| **the same ingredient row twice in `ingredients:`** | 17 |

And the duplication is not confined to anchored records — **16 further records** have it
with no anchors at all. YAML anchors are just how `yaml.dump` renders a repeated row when
the two happen to be the same Python object.

## The defect

33 records list an ingredient twice at the same concentration, so anything that sums or
iterates `ingredients:` reads them as double-strength. `for_dsm_14290.yaml` carried
Tryptone 10 g/l, Yeast extract 5 g/l and Sodium chloride 10 g/l **twice each**.

## Narrow on purpose

A row is dropped only when identical to another in **every** field — name, concentration,
term, notes, supplier_catalog. Removing an exact copy cannot lose information.

**21 rows across 8 records repeat a name and concentration but differ** in `notes`,
`supplier_catalog` or `term`. Those are left alone and reported. They look like one
ingredient recorded from two sources, but collapsing them means choosing which provenance
survives — a curation call, and a blind dedup would silently keep whichever came first. A
test pins that they aren't touched.

**104 rows removed across 44 records** (61 normalized + 43 merged). Residual
fully-identical duplicate rows: **0**.

## Found while canarying

`sbbm.yaml` listed `Make up to 1 litre with distilled water. For agar add` as a 15 G_PER_L
ingredient — a preparation instruction parsed as a component, with a concentration that
probably belongs to the agar. Filed as #273; not fixed here.

## Verification

- `validate-strict`: 0 ERROR rows over 15,877 files
- `pytest`: 1,181 passed, 5 new
- both corpora, so the #266 derived-corpus check stays green
- canary first, before fan-out

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: Correct #181 (15 of 17 were false positives) and triage the 428 media with no composition (#175)
items.body:
Both issues were overstated, for the same reason: a record's composition lives in
`ingredients` **and** `solutions`, and both measurements read only the first.

## #181 — 17 records was really 2

A stock-supplied antibiotic is recorded as a SOLUTION. `lb_rifampicin_medium`
carries `"Rifampicin solution (50 mg/ml)*"` under `solutions`; its `ingredients`
genuinely are plain LB. The audit merged in #187 checked only `ingredients` and
called **15 complete records defective**.

This matters beyond the count. The Edison probe that prompted #181 declined to
classify that medium as SELECTIVE because *"the supplied ingredient list contains
no rifampicin entry"* — accurate about the ingredient list it was handed, which is
exactly the slot the research template passes. **The record was never defective;
the view of it was partial.** My audit then reproduced the same partial view and
concluded the corpus was broken — a tool built to avoid confident wrong answers
producing one.

Found by asking whether the missing agents were recoverable from `data/raw/togo`.
Every one was there, which raised the question of why the import had dropped
them. It hadn't.

`composition_terms()` now spans `ingredients`, `solutions` and nested
`solutions[].composition`. **Baseline 17 → 2.**

The 2 survivors are both DSMZ Medium 309 via KOMODO and DSMZ. Neither has a
`solutions` entry, and the local mediadive extraction of medium 309 lacks the
neomycin too — and the agar, despite the name "NEOMYCIN AGAR". That gap is
upstream, not in this import.

## #175 — 463 records was really 428

35 carry their whole composition under `solutions`.

```
327  KOMODO ModelSEED, nothing in either slot
101  a single placeholder ingredient
```

**162 are named like a stock solution, not a medium** — "Trace element solution
(medium 929)", "Solution C, medium 1275", "10 x M9 salts". These are solutions
imported as media records, not media missing a recipe.

### The trap this report exists to document

217 of them cite a medium number resolving to a local composition file, which
looks like a large automatic fix.

`Trace element solution (medium 1072)` means the solution defined **inside**
medium 1072. And `dsmz_1072`'s composition is the whole medium — KH2PO4, MgSO4,
NH4Cl, KCl, CaCl2, Na-acetate, yeast extract, casamino acids, NaCl at 15 g/L —
including a line reading `Trace element solution (see below) 2.0ml`, which is the
part actually wanted.

Applying it would write a full medium's recipe into 217 solution records:
plausible, round-trips, validates, wrong. #166 at scale.

The dump is independently unreliable — `dsmz_929` records its `medium_name` as
"NaCl" (its first component), and `dsmz_1275` lists `"Solution A:"` as a 0.65 g
component. It is `pdf_tabular_parsing` output, not curated.

The report records that a candidate exists; **a test asserts no column proposes it
as the composition.**

Refs #181, #175.

items.title: Refresh 120k legacy MediaIngredientMech links to CHEBI keying
items.body:
## Why
MediaIngredientMech deprecated its `MediaIngredientMech:NNNNNN` id scheme and re-keyed curated ingredients by CHEBI (current canonical file carries **0** of the old ids). **9,695 CultureMech records** still referenced that dead scheme via `mediaingredientmech_term`.

## What — id-safe refresh-replace
`scripts/migrate_legacy_mim_to_chebi.py` rewrites legacy links to `mediaingredientmech_chebi_term`:

- **CHEBI present (~99.8%)** — the ingredient already carries its own CHEBI `term`; if that CHEBI is in current MIM, replace the legacy field using the ingredient's **own** CHEBI id + label. MIM's `preferred_term` is **not** imported (it diverges ~21%), so no ingredient labels change semantically.
- **CHEBI gap (~203)** — legacy link, no CHEBI term → name/synonym match against current MIM; on a hit, also set the ingredient's `term` (closes the grounding gap) + add the link. (Verified: "Vitamine B12" → CHEBI:176843.)
- **Unmappable (1,509 records)** — CHEBI not in current MIM and no name match → legacy field left intact.

## Result
- **9,671 files changed, 120,029 links refreshed.**
- Re-emitted with PyYAML `safe_dump` (the corpus's original settings) → unchanged fields round-trip **byte-identically**, diffs are per-field. The +56k net insertions are the per-file `curation_history` entries.
- All 9,671 migrated files parse; sampled + corpus-wide checks confirm **0** non-CHEBI ids in the new field.
- Reviewers: review **the script + a few sample diffs + the report**, not all 9,671 files (mechanical, uniform transform).

## Byproducts folded in
- **203-gap fix** — no-CHEBI stragglers grounded via MIM name match.
- **Grounding-audit flag** — `data/import_tracking/reports/mim_grounding_divergences.tsv` (500 CHEBI ids where CultureMech vs MIM labels differ). Mostly benign formatting (`Na-ascorbate`), with a thin tail of real issues (e.g. `CHEBI:37583` phosphate confusion; 2 pyridoxine/pyridoxamine mislabels) for `audit-schema-gaps`.

## Dependency
⚠️ **Stacked on #34** (uses the `MediaIngredientMechChebiTerm` schema field). Base retargets to `main` once #34 merges.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: 226 media have no usable composition (was 463, then 428 — 202 were mis-typed stock solutions)
items.body:
## Surfaced by the review-need ranking

Two adjacent failure modes, both meaning the record carries no recipe at all:

```
362  records with zero ingredients
101  records whose only ingredient text is "See source for composition"
---
463  records (4.2% of 11,094 media) with no usable composition
```

The 101 are strikingly uniform — every one uses that exact string, so this is one import path, not scattered curation gaps.

## Why this was not visible before

`prioritize_deep_research_candidates.py` **hard-filters zero-ingredient records** before scoring, and rewards recipe completeness thereafter. That is correct for its purpose — ranking where deep research will pay off — but it means the damaged tail is invisible to the only ranking the repo had. These 463 records have never appeared at the top of anything.

`validate-strict` does not catch them either: `ingredients` is not required, so an empty list is schema-valid.

## Included in the 463

`bacterial/test_medium_123.yaml` — `original_name: "Test Medium 123"`, sole ingredient "See source for composition", holding `CultureMech:000306`. A test fixture that reached the production corpus and was assigned a real id.

## What to decide

Per group, and they may differ:

1. **Recoverable?** The `notes` on several say "Imported from BacDive cultivation data", so the source may still have the composition and a re-import could fill them.
2. **Or honestly empty?** If the source genuinely has no composition, the record should say so — a `data_quality_flags` entry — rather than carrying one fake ingredient that pollutes every text scan. The placeholder string already matches ingredient searches, which is how it turned up here.
3. **Or spurious?** `test_medium_123` should probably not exist. Deleting it means retiring a CultureMech id, which is a separate decision (cf. #144).

## Reproduce

```
just score-review-need --top 40
```

They occupy the 70-80 band. Ranking, signals and weights are in `scripts/score_review_need.py`.
